clue.text: Menial worker follows lad around Germany

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them

indicators.note: around means one word wraps itself about the other, holding it inside

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A lowly employee trails a young man on a trip round Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' is a verb in the surface, but it supplies a word on its own; D is Germany's international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is British slang for someone given all the drudge jobs nobody else wants.

clue.text: Edward lifted coin up to scratch

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Edward pockets a coin, which is hardly acceptable behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means acceptable or of a satisfactory standard, an idiom match for up to scratch.

clue.text: Old slug I disturbed grasping a flower

indicators.note: grasping means holding within, so one letter is taken inside the others
something disturbed has been thrown out of its settled order

explanation.surface: A gardener disturbs an old slug clinging to a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a garden plant with tall spikes of blooms, grown from corms.

clue.text: Courage from supporter? Decidedly

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
very and decidedly both mean extremely

explanation.surface: A question of whether a fan is truly brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but it is an item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery is the quality of facing danger without fear, the same thing as courage.

clue.text: Barking like a Dalmation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mad, as in barking mad
second meaning: covered in dots, as the spotted dog is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' suggests a dog, which the Dalmatian (misspelt in the clue) seems to confirm, but it is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is informal for slightly mad, and can be read literally as marked with spots.

clue.text: Really bad description of candle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: evil, morally very bad
second meaning: having a wick, as a candle does

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful coinage: a candle has a wick, so it is 'wick-ed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means evil in ordinary use, and can be read literally as equipped with a burning thread.

clue.text: Type of coffee isn't drunk by social worker

indicators.note: drunk means staggering about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word without the apostrophe, mixed
ants are social insects and include worker ants

explanation.surface: A social worker turns down a cup of a particular coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a care professional, but it is an insect that lives in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant coffee is a kind made from soluble powder or granules rather than ground beans.

clue.text: Tango drink upset artist

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: Tango is T in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A painter is upset by the drink served at a tango evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Klimt was an Austrian painter, famous for The Kiss.

clue.text: Fool, perhaps, heartless editor abandoned

indicators.note: heartless means with the heart taken out, so a central letter goes

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, an example of a sweet course

explanation.surface: A foolish, unfeeling editor walks out on the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit folded into cream; dropping one middle S from DESSERT leaves DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted means left behind or forsaken, the same as abandoned.

clue.text: Bishop on Zoom allowed jewellery

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to zoom is to race along

explanation.surface: A bishop on a Zoom call was permitted to wear his bling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zoom' looks like the video app, but it is just a verb for speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn round the wrist, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Crass architect and I redesigned properties

indicators.note: something redesigned has had its parts rearranged into a new layout

explanation.surface: A tasteless architect and the speaker remodel some houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properties' looks like buildings to suit the architect, but it means qualities or traits.
explanation.definitionFit: Properties in the sense of distinguishing qualities or traits are characteristics.

clue.text: Navy tie at sea shows lack of sophistication

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wearing a navy tie on a ship marks a sailor as unworldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or a want of worldly experience, the opposite of sophistication.

clue.text: Vessel — and what might go under one

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ship that sails along the shore
second meaning: a mat placed beneath a glass or cup, another sort of vessel

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to 'vessel', switching from a ship to a drinking vessel such as a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaster is both a ship trading along a coastline and a small mat set beneath a drink.

clue.text: Show willing, amuse oneself and dance

parts.note: to play is to amuse oneself
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A list of the ways to enjoy oneself at a party: be keen, have fun, dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for cooperating, showing one is willing to go along.

clue.text: A quiet dog possibly bites both ends off, showing hunger

indicators.note: with both ends off, the first and final letters are cut away

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A silent dog nips off both ends of something, showing it is famished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bites' reads as the verb of the dog, but it is the word to trim: shorn of its first and last letters it leaves ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a desire to eat, which is what hunger is.

clue.text: Backing short European ceasefire

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Supporting a brief European halt to fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The backing applies only to 'short', not to the European letter that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement between enemies to stop fighting for a while.

clue.text: Even nan coughed badly, lacking oxygen

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out jumbled
lacking means going without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Grandma coughed hard, short of air, even so.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from NAN COUGHED, then rearrange the rest. 'Even' looks like an adverb, but it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even stays steady and level, constant or not altered.

clue.text: Prisoner on trial with singular struggles

explanation.surface: A convict in the dock with one particular case fights on.
explanation.definitionFit: Contests are fights or competitions, in which people strive against each other.

clue.text: Watering hole guarded by buffalo as I speak

indicators.note: something guarded by these words is held within them, sitting inside the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the ending of the first word, then the next two words, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A speaker notes that buffalo keep a drinking spot under watch.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where animals and travellers find water.

clue.text: Drink left for bear

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drink set aside for a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning hold up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to carry its weight, the same as supporting it.

clue.text: Forbearance from sick people on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the sound matters

parts.note: sick people under a doctor's care are patients

explanation.surface: Tolerance shown by ill callers to a phone-in show.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance is self-control and tolerance in the face of provocation, which is patience.

clue.text: Go off and walk in Devon river

indicators.note: in places the walking word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river flowing through Devon, an English county
to plod is to walk heavily

explanation.surface: Head out for a stroll beside a West Country river.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its short river is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that goes off detonates, which is to explode.

clue.text: I object about National Trust's plan

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first part goes round the trust's letters

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
NT abbreviates the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the heritage body's development scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is the noun meaning aim or goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it in mind as a purpose, which is to plan it.

clue.text: Better tent oddly discarded — this gets blown in the wind

definitions.text: this gets blown in the wind

parts.note: to trump is to better or outdo

indicators.note: throwing away the odd-numbered letters leaves just the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: Pitching a better tent so it does not blow away in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wind' looks like weather, but it is the wind section of an orchestra, which is blown.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is a brass instrument played by blowing, and belongs among the wind instruments.

clue.text: American group losing weight exercising

indicators.note: losing means going without, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a wing is a faction or group within a party

explanation.surface: A US fitness class shedding pounds through workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' suggests a workout, but it is meant as in exercising a right.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a power or right is to put it to use, so exercising means using.

clue.text: Conservative with appropriate answer now leader

parts.note: in means fashionable, of the moment

explanation.surface: A Tory with the right response is now in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the leader of a team, ship or military company.

clue.text: Low-priced clubs? Great deal!

parts.note: C abbreviates clubs, the card suit
a heap is a great deal, a lot

explanation.surface: Golf clubs at a bargain price, what a great deal!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great deal' sounds like a bargain, but it means a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap describes something costing little money, a plain synonym for inexpensive.

clue.text: Host feeling put out admitting old gaffe

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the rest
out here means out of order or disrupted, so the letters get reshuffled

explanation.surface: A party host, feeling offended, confesses to an old social blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as one phrase meaning offended, but 'put' is fodder and 'out' the signal; O joins the other letters before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue is an unintended remark, a small verbal blunder or gaffe.

clue.text: Insults no student's spots

indicators.note: no means without, so the following item is dropped

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: Mocking a pupil's acne is out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like pimples, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, so sights works as a verb meaning notices.

clue.text: Fantastic swims going west around lake draw to a close

indicators.note: around means the reversed word encloses what follows
going west in an across clue means right to left, the word read backwards

parts.note: to end is to draw to a close

explanation.surface: Brilliant swims heading west round a lake are coming to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, west is leftwards, so the swims are read backwards before wrapping the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid and fantastic are both informal words of praise for something excellent.
